I was curious about this movie because of a ridiculously enticing trailer that had Leonard Cohen 's " You want it Darker " playing over it. The lyrics seemed perfect for the images I was seeing on screen : "There's a lover in the story, but the story's still the same - There's a lullaby for suffering and a paradox to blame - I didn't know I had permission to murder and to maim - You want it darker ? We kill the flame." Well, I wish I had never seen that trailer. Because, truly, nothing was remotely as good as what those 2 minutes teased and suggested. [Spoilers ahead] ( Before I start - I know that this is adapted from a book, and I've seen, as always, people say that the book was better, but know that I am not aware of the differences bewteen the original story and its adaptation.) THE PLOT : Against her father's rules, Maren, 18, sneaks out of the house to join a slumber party with 3 other girls. She must go back ' before 6AM ' she says, just in case. We barely have any time to get to know any character, our protagonist included, that she bites off her friend's finger. She comes back home, bloodied, banging on the front door. Her dad, instantly, gives her a " You didn't ", confirming this wasn't a first. " You have 3 minutes to pack before we leave and the police comes ". This clearly isn't a first. Maren and her father flee, and start a new life, all over again. But soon enough, her dad disappears. Maren is left all alone with her 'issue', with, as a goodbye, a message on a cassette to listen to, and a birth certificate with her estranged Mother's name. Here starts the girl's journey to find the latter, and herself alongside. THE CAST : Probably my very first problem with this movie - None of the characters I felt invested in, and the second roles shone way more than the 2 protagonists, Maren ( Taylor Russell ) and Lee ( Timothée Chalamet ). They are lifeless, boring, unconvincing. They have about as much chemistry as water and oil do. We're somehow supposed to believe those two love each other to death in such a short time, and while I know young love can be intense, this is not what's accurately represented here. Lee and Maren are together by default , because ' they're the same '. That's all. We don't see them having any real meaningful conversations, we just see them be . Which again, would be fine if they had that spark, but they just do not. THE SFX : The very few gory scenes are very well executed and I honestly wished there would have been more. For a movie which the literal main theme is cannibalism, there is almost none of it on screen (or off, for that matter). THE SOUND : Oh man, that fucking acoustic guitar. Those damn 4 accords we keep hearing all throughout the movie just about drove me crazy. Every time a conversation ended, or an important scene did, we had those zoom outs accompanied by that guitar trying to be melancholic. Of what , exactly ? I couldn't tell you. This movie desperately tries to be mellow, bittersweet and contemplative, but it fails in all regards. It's just slow and vapid. You should have seen the face I made when I recognized Trent Reznor 's voice at one point (in what I learned was the title song). I still cannot believe this literal genius of a composer did this score. If it wasn't for (obviously) hearing his voice; I would have never associated Reznor (nor Atticus Ross) to this movie. THE CINEMATOGRAPHY : This is the only good part of this movie, the way it looks. If you look at the trailers, it is absolutely beautiful, the dialogue sounds heartfelt, the feelings of the characters seem intense, it looks so good. Sadly, when spread accross two excruciating hours and eleven minutes, the cinematography isn't going to be enough. Despite it being gorgeous, I still have some gripes with it; to me, the filming lacked any kind of dynamism - it actually does feel like a 2h music video at times. And believe me, I love contemplative films. This one just wasn't it for me. IN THE END : Bones and All seems like a failed promise. From the moment Maren meets Lee, the movie ironically goes downhill. It wants to be controversial but just doesn't go far enough, then take that back and tries throwing us off with disgusting, shocking  characters, but they're never an actual threat. It all falls short. And every time the protagonists do something reprehensible, they are excused, justified by their ' nature ' and the very quick and basic remorse Maren sometimes shows. Their personal set of morals is discussable too; as the only person we see the couple feeding on together is a gay guy that Lee kills in a cornfield (only after sex, for some reason), but when Maren discovers he was married to a woman with a kid, suddenly, she freaks out. Ok girl. In the end, what bothers me most probably is the parallel this film obviously tries to make, using cannibalism as an analogy. The poster says " You can't run from who you are ", pretty much making them being cannibals their whole identity, making it unquestionnable, while the movie itself fights tooth and nails to make them appear desperately human. Final note : 2/10 . Bones and All had -everything-, and I truly mean everything , on paper, to appeal to me. But I found nothing enjoyable aside from the visuals, and then again, not for 2+ hours. As I often say to myself, " This would have been a great 40min short ".

Träumer Kino der schönsten und seltsamsten Sorte, das vielleicht gar nicht so das großartige Werk mit Metaphern aufgeladen ist, sondern eher eine kleine sympatische Kuriosität. Bones and All würde ist ein wenig bizarr und voller Gegensätze, aber im Kern würde ich sagen, es ist eine Außenseiter-Story, wie man ein Leben lebt mit einem let's call it "Lebensstil", der als problematisch angesehen wird. Dazu gehört sowas wie, dass sobald das Leben unerträglich wird, man Gleichgesinnte findet, die einem Halt geben, das Konzept fatalistischer Liebe und natürlich ganz viele Bilder, die ein Midwest-Roadtrip so gemütlich machen, wie man ihn sich nur vorstellt. Der krasse Gegensatz ist dann natürlich der Part, wo Maren und ihre vielen Bekanntschaften Menschen essen, aber auch das wird weirdly eklig faszinierend eingefangen und wirkt gegen Ende fast schon karthatisch. So ganz konnte ich mir keinen Reim auf diesen Aspekt der Geschichte machen, aber wie gesagt ist der Film sehr laid back und hat mir eher etwas Komfort mit dem Gefühl gegeben, wenn man im Leben einsam ist und sich anders und missverstanden fühlt. In gewisser Weise ist es auch ein Coming of Age Film. Aus Marens Perspektive beginnt ihr Leben erst so richtig, als ihr Vater sie zurücklässt und sie die Welt auf eigene Faust, ohne einen Vormund, entdeckt. Sie lernt noch viele andere Menschen wie sie kennen und irgendwann wird klar, dass im ganzen Land eine Art Community existiert, die ihre Dränge unterschiedlich ausleben, aber alle versteckt vor der allgemeinen Gesellschaft leben. An der Stelle geht der Lebensstil von Maren und Lee auch perfekt mit der im Midwest geprägten Armut einher. Man kann sich nirgends niederlassen, entwickeln, ist generell misstrauisch und kann morden und rauben wie es einem beliebt, weils eh kaum jemand nachverfolgt. Am Ende ist Bones and All für mich weniger Horror oder große Metapher als einfach ein stimmungsvoller Roadtrip über Einsamkeit, das Heranwachsen und das Bedürfnis, irgendwo dazuzugehören. Nicht jede Idee geht für mich komplett auf, aber Luca Guadagnino erschafft daraus so eine eigenartige Wohlfühlmelancholie, dass ich mich in der seltsamen Perspektive von Maren und Lee total verloren habe.

Beautiful film. Luca did such a good job at balancing romance and horror, which are two polar opposites. The feeding scenes of the eaters were disgusting and incredibly gruesome, but watching it still felt warm somehow. Maybe it’s the muted colors and the strings that recurred throughout the film. My God, it was beautiful. I can’t believe I didn’t appreciate it as much before as I do now. Whatever they’re doing, killing and eating people, is morally wrong and just blatantly evil, but I can’t help but root for Maren and Lee. Whatever they had felt so calm and true, and they were really only like that with each other. ‘Di ko magets mga nagsasabing wala silang chemistry, to be honest kasi … kita niyo ba mga halikan scenes nila hahaha? I wanted the film to end when they had normal lives. They looked so happy. But the ending just made everything so much more painful to watch, andddd I’d watch it over and over again. It was so beautiful. What they had was bound to end eventually. Sabi nga nila, “Let’s be them for a while .” It wasn’t meant to last because they were pretending all along. I do wonder if they really had a choice, though. Maren actively decides not to eat people, but she eventually succumbs to it. Maybe cannibalism is intrinsic to them. Maybe they can stop for a while, eat their hands or whatnot in hopes of saving the people they love, but it all surfaces eventually, which is heartbreaking because it gets in the way of so many beautiful things. Or maybe… maybe they had a way out; they just didn’t know how. Siguro dito hindi magiging applicable ‘yong “if he wanted to, he would” hahahah. Ano ‘yun, final act of love niya ay ipinakain sarili niya para maging part siya ni Maren forever? Alam ko namang madali lang para sa kanila, well, for most of them at least, na mag move on sa mga kinakain nila, pero kung ako si Maren, ‘di talaga ako makakausad after niyan. Hay buhay talaga. What a painfully beautiful ending.
